Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Please organize the work for Tuesday, 18 June, from the 06:10 opening until the 14:40 handover. The desk is beside the north gate, and it handles bags for both the 08:00 island sailing and the 11:30 harbor sailing. Keep those sailings separate in the wording, because their collection points are not the same. I want the request to be practical for the two desk attendants, not a general description of ferry service.

At opening, ask the first attendant to check the counter, the tag printer, and the locked storage room before accepting bags. There are 18 tagged bags already in storage from the overnight shift; that number is the opening count, not a new batch to tag. The second attendant should compare those bags with the paper ledger and mark any difference for the supervisor to review. Do not state that the count has been confirmed, because no one has checked it yet. There are also 6 unclaimed tags in the drawer. Those are blank tags, not six bags, and the attendants should keep them available for new luggage.

The first sailing has 12 reservations listed for oversized luggage, but that is a reservation count rather than a count of bags already delivered. Ask staff to verify each arriving item against its passenger's claim receipt and to put an oversized bag in the marked area only after the receipt matches. The marked area has room for 9 bags. If more than 9 oversized bags arrive before the 08:00 departure, ask an attendant to stop adding bags there and call the supervisor for placement instructions. Do not imply that the extra space or another storage room has already been approved. The 11:30 sailing has a different collection point, at the east-side bench, and its bags must not be mixed with the north-gate group.

Please include the instruction to attach the current desk note to the shift record. Use this exact filename on its own line so it can be copied without confusion:
north-gate-notes.md
The desk note is for the shift record, not a passenger handout. The record should also say who completed the opening count and when it was checked. If the two attendants find a mismatch, they should record the number they actually see and leave the review field for the supervisor; they should not adjust the ledger themselves. The morning lead said, “Write down what is in front of you, not what you expect to find.” Keep that quotation as a spoken reminder, and do not turn it into a claim that the opening count is correct.

For the routine during the morning, describe a short check at 07:15 and another at 10:45. At each check, staff should confirm the labels remain readable, the two sailing groups stay apart, and the aisle beside the counter is clear. These are scheduled check times, not deadlines for loading. The terminal team has 3 luggage carts assigned to this desk, and they should be returned to the marked bay after use. Two handheld radios are available; one stays with the attendant at the counter and the other goes with the person moving bags. Ask staff to report a radio that will not hold a charge, but do not say that either radio is faulty now.

1. For the 08:00 island sailing, keep the north-gate group together and use the passenger claim receipt to check each bag before placing it in the marked oversized area. The 12 reservations do not mean 12 bags have arrived, and the area capacity is 9 bags.
2. For the 11:30 harbor sailing, keep its luggage at the east-side bench collection point and separate from the 08:00 group. The bench is the collection point; it is not another locked storage room.
3. At 12:20, ask the second attendant to reconcile the paper ledger with the bags still held at the desk. Record the number present and note any bag collected since opening. Do not erase an earlier entry; add the correction with the time and the initials of the attendant who made it.
4. Before the 14:40 handover, list open issues, including any count difference, missing claim receipt, or damaged tag, and identify which sailing group is involved. The next shift needs the facts needed to locate the item, not an assumption about how the issue will be resolved.

There is a condition for the later checks that needs to stay clear. If the ferry office announces a delay for either sailing before 10:45, ask the desk lead to confirm whether the collection point should remain in use, and record the instruction with the announcement time. Until that confirmation arrives, staff should keep the two groups separate and should not move a bag to a different collection point. If no delay is announced before 10:45, continue the ordinary check and record that it took place. This is a conditional instruction, not a statement that a delay has been announced.

The desk supervisor also asked for a brief note about passenger questions, but the attendants should record only questions that affect finding or releasing a bag. For example, note if a passenger gives a different spelling from the tag or cannot produce the claim receipt; include the sailing time and the tag number if one is visible. Do not write down payment-card details or extra personal information. If the passenger says, “My bag was left by the east bench,” record the words as the passenger's report and check the location before changing any entry. That quotation does not establish that the bag is there.

At handover, ask the morning attendants to leave the counter clear, return the 3 carts to their bay, and pass both radios to the incoming team, with any charging problem noted. Have them state which ledger entries still need review and whether the supervisor was contacted about any overflow or discrepancy. The afternoon team should be able to distinguish confirmed observations from items awaiting review. Keep the 14:40 time as the handover time, and do not describe the desk as closed then; the request is only to prepare the morning handover information. Include the status of both sailing groups and the location where each is being held, even if there has been no change since the prior check.
